newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady on Thursday with dealers monitoring this week's gains in Chicago Board of Trade corn futures.
Dealers said the runup in corn was not expected to affect nearby midds markets but would impact midds in the long term.
"The runup in corn is causing the deferred markets to firm up," a Kansas dealer said.
He added some pastures in Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas were dry. But livestock was still feeding on grass.
A North Texas dealer said his area needed rain.
"Pastures were burning up," he said, referring to the high temperatures in parts of Texas.
In Minneapolis, a broker said buying was limited but noted a little more interest for the deferreds.
The northeastern market was holding steady. "The feed mixers seem to be in fine shape," a Buffalo dealer said.
"Everyone seems to be pretty well set for next week, both sellers and buyers. So it's a thin market, holding its own," he said.
The Pennsylvania market gave up $1 or $2 earlier this week, trading at about $81, he added.
